description: Runner-side automatic cleanup of completed workflow workspaces: server exposes cleanup policy + terminal-status reachability; runner adds an active-workspace registry, terminal-state detection (event push + convergence backstop), and a retention/budget eviction loop with pre-delete guards.

tasks.title: Server exposes cleanup policy and routes workflow terminal status to the owning runner
tasks.description: Add an optional cleanupPolicy (retentionDays, storageBudgetBytes, storageTargetWatermarkBytes) to WorkDispatchResponse so the runner reads it on every poll. Add POST /api/runner/{runnerId}/workflow-runs/status accepting a list of workflow run ids and returning their current lifecycle status (terminal vs non-terminal) for runner convergence. Route workflow terminal events (completed/stopped/failed) to the owning runner by invoking a new SignalR method ReceiveWorkflowRunStatus({ workflowRunId, status }) via the runner assignment state. The server must not scan runner filesystems or own a deletion queue.
acceptanceCriteria: WorkDispatchResponse carries cleanupPolicy with retentionDays, storageBudgetBytes, storageTargetWatermarkBytes (nullable/unlimited sentinels supported); runner poll response includes it.

POST /api/runner/{runnerId}/workflow-runs/status returns { [runId]: status } only for the requested run ids and distinguishes terminal (completed/stopped/failed) from non-terminal (running/paused/awaiting approval) states.
When a workflow run reaches a terminal state and its owning runner is connected, the server invokes ReceiveWorkflowRunStatus on that runner with the run id and terminal status.
Server has no filesystem scanning, cleanup queue, or runner-deletion path beyond the existing manual POST /issues/{n}/cleanup route.
Server unit/integration tests cover policy propagation, the batch status endpoint (incl. unknown/empty run ids), and terminal-event routing to the assigned runner.
tasks.output: Server changes: WorkDispatchResponse + cleanup policy config, runner batch status endpoint, terminal-event→runner SignalR routing; with passing server tests.
tasks.notes: Ship additive; runners ignore unknown fields. Policy defaults to null/disabled so no eviction occurs until configured. Decide server config scope (system-wide vs per-project) during implementation (see design Open Questions).

tasks.title: Runner active workspace registry with materialize/verify/manual-cleanup registration hooks
tasks.description: Add a runner-local workspace registry persisted at <runnerRoot>/.mohist/runner-state/workspaces.json, keyed by workflowRunId, recording issueId, issueNumber, workflowRunId, resolved workspacePath, phase (active/eligible), materializedAt, terminalAt. Load into RunnerHost at startup and write-through atomically on every mutation. Register/refresh an active entry on WorkspaceManager.materialize() success and on verify() reuse; delete the entry when the manual RemoveWorkspace handler removes a directory. Keep the on-disk .mohist/workspace.json marker exactly identity-only (issueId, issueNumber, workflowRunId) — no timestamps are written to the marker.
acceptanceCriteria: After a successful materialize, a registry entry keyed by workflowRunId exists in phase 'active' with materializedAt set and the resolved workspacePath.
Registry is persisted and reloaded on runner restart; active entries remain active until a terminal transition is observed.
Manual RemoveWorkspace success removes the matching registry entry, keeping the registry consistent with disk reality.
The .mohist/workspace.json marker still contains exactly issueId, issueNumber, workflowRunId and no timestamp fields.
Runner unit tests cover registry load/save atomicity, materialize registration, verify refresh, restart reload, and manual-cleanup entry removal.
tasks.output: Runner registry module (storage + in-memory cache) wired into WorkspaceManager.materialize/verify and the RemoveWorkspace handler; with passing runner tests.
tasks.notes: Registry is runner-local runtime state, not domain truth. safeRemove must tolerate an already-missing directory (treat as removed, delete the entry). Independent of server work — usable standalone for tracking active workspaces.

tasks.title: Runner terminal-state detection via event push and convergence backstop
tasks.description: Handle the server's ReceiveWorkflowRunStatus SignalR method to transition the matching registry entry from active to eligible and stamp terminalAt (idempotent — already-eligible entries are not re-stamped). Add a convergence backstop that, on startup, on SignalR reconnect, and on a periodic timer, queries POST /api/runner/{runnerId}/workflow-runs/status exclusively for entries still in phase 'active' and transitions any server-reported-terminal run to eligible. The runner must never scan the server's full workflow history or re-query already-eligible entries.
acceptanceCriteria: On ReceiveWorkflowRunStatus for a terminal status, the matching active registry entry transitions to eligible with terminalAt set; an already-eligible entry is not re-transitioned or re-stamped.
On startup, reconnect, and the periodic timer, the runner queries the server only for active registry entries and transitions server-reported-terminal runs to eligible.
Convergence never enumerates or queries workflow runs that have no active registry entry on this runner (no full-history scan).
Non-terminal statuses (running/paused/awaiting approval) leave the entry active.
Runner unit/integration tests cover push-driven transition, idempotent re-transition, convergence on reconnect/periodic tick, and the no-full-history-scan guarantee.
tasks.output: Runner ReceiveWorkflowRunStatus handler + convergence query wired into RunnerHost lifecycle (startup, onReconnected, periodic timer); with passing runner tests.
tasks.notes: Push is a latency optimization only; correctness must not depend on it — the convergence query is the authoritative catch-all for missed events.

tasks.title: Runner automatic cleanup: retention, storage-budget eviction, and pre-delete guards
tasks.description: Add a runCleanupLoop in RunnerHost that, on each tick, evicts eligible workspaces older than the configured retention window (measured from terminalAt) and, when usage exceeds the configured storage budget, evicts eligible workspaces in ascending terminalAt order until usage drops below the target watermark. Each removal runs a shared safeRemove that verifies the target path is contained under runnerRoot AND the on-disk marker's workflowRunId matches the registry entry before deleteDirectory, aborting (and leaving both directory and entry intact) on any mismatch, missing marker, or out-of-root path. The loop must never evict active entries and must not collide with in-flight work for a run. Read cleanupPolicy from the poll response (T-001); when policy fields are null/unlimited the corresponding eviction is disabled.
acceptanceCriteria: Eligible workspaces past the retention window are removed; those within the window are kept; retention disabled (null) disables age-based eviction.
When usage exceeds the storage budget, eligible workspaces are evicted earliest-terminalAt-first until usage is at or below the target watermark; active entries are never evicted.

Every automatic removal passes both pre-delete guards (path under runnerRoot AND on-disk marker workflowRunId matches the registry entry); out-of-root, missing-marker, or mismatched-marker removals are aborted and leave the directory and entry intact.
No active/pending/paused/awaiting-approval/identity-mismatched workspace is removed by automatic cleanup.
Automatic cleanup removes only the workspace directory under runnerRoot; no workflow run, issue, event, artifact, session, DB record, or repo cache is deleted.
The existing manual cleanup entry continues to work unchanged alongside automatic cleanup.

Runner unit/integration tests cover retention eviction ordering, budget eviction to watermark with earliest-first ordering, each pre-delete guard rejection (out-of-root, marker mismatch, missing marker), active-entry protection, and unchanged manual-cleanup behavior.
tasks.output: Runner runCleanupLoop with safeRemove guards (reusing isUnderRunnerRoot/readMarker) consuming cleanupPolicy from the poll response; with passing runner tests.
tasks.notes: safeRemove reuses isUnderRunnerRoot (runner-signalr.ts) and readMarker (workspace.ts) unchanged. Budget usage computation should be lazy and cached between ticks to avoid expensive du on every tick. Ship with policy defaulting to disabled so no workspaces are removed until a policy is configured.
